finalText:
**Merge** ties two branches together with a merge commit. You get a full history of both paths. The timeline branches and joins again — you can see that work happened in parallel.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch. You get a straight line of changes, as if you'd written them one after the other. History is rewritten, not added to.

**When to merge:** When the branch is shared or already public. When you want to see that two things happened side by side. When you're pulling someone else's work into your own.

**When to rebase:** On your own local branch, before pushing. When you want a clean, readable log. When your commits were based on an older version and you want them on the latest.

The rule: never rebase what's shared. Once other people have pulled your commits, rewriting them breaks their history. Rebase feels cleaner, but merge is safer.
